Validate Weight Outlier Methods with Artificial Errors

Source: R/validate.R
validate_outliers.Rd

Add artificial errors to body weight records that passed the checks, then run clean_weight() with each outlier method and measure how many artificial errors are found, how many good records are removed, and how far ADG moves from the ADG of the clean records.

validate_outliers(
  visits,
  qc = qc_config(),
  methods = list(`track+rlm+loess` = c("track", "rlm", "loess"), track = "track", rlm =
    "rlm", loess = "loess", `rlm+loess` = c("rlm", "loess"), stl = "stl", sd = "sd"),
  rate = 0.05,
  size = c(3, 15),
  direction = c("both", "down", "up"),
  reps = 3,
  max_pigs = NULL,
  seed = 1,
  reference = c("consensus", "qc"),
  verbose = 1,
  cores = 1
)

Arguments

visits

Result of prep_visits().

qc

QC settings from qc_config(): every setting except weight_outlier and weight_track.

methods

Named list of outlier method sets to compare. Each element holds values of weight_outlier, plus "track" to track the weight back from the end of the test first (weight_track = TRUE); sets without "track" run without tracking. "track" alone is the tracking without any other method.

rate

Share of clean records that receive an artificial error. Default 0.05.

size

Range of the error size in kg. Default c(3, 15).

direction

"both" (default): errors are added or subtracted at random; "down": weights too low only (pig partly on the scale); "up": too high only (two pigs on the scale).

reps

Number of repetitions. Default 3.

max_pigs

Use a random sample of at most this many pigs, to save time on large data (a few hundred pigs are enough). Default NULL: all.

seed

Random seed, for reproducible results.

reference

Which records count as clean, i.e. receive the artificial errors and give the reference ADG: "consensus" (default) the records kept by qc and by every method in methods, so that no method is favoured; "qc" the records kept by qc (before 1.5.0), which favours the method of qc.

verbose

0 (silent), 1 (summary and progress, default).

cores

Number of CPU cores for clean_weight() and calc_adg().

Value

A list of class ppt_validation with

  • summary: one row per method: sensitivity (share of artificial errors found), false_positive_rate (share of clean records removed), precision, adg_bias and adg_rmse (g/d, against the ADG of the clean records), adg_spearman (rank correlation) and n_pigs;

  • per_rep: the same for each repetition;

  • settings.

Details

The clean records are found by the methods themselves, so they are not free of error. With reference = "consensus" a record is clean only when no method flags it: every method starts from the same records, and a method is not judged "wrong" for flagging a record that qc happened to keep. The reference ADG is the ADG of the clean records, without any outlier method. The row none shows the result when only weight_range is applied (errors that push a weight outside it are still found).

Errors placed at random times shift single records but hardly move a growth curve fitted to hundreds of records, so ADG differences between methods are small; they mostly reflect which good records each method removes.

Examples

visits <- prep_visits(nedap, verbose = 0)
w <- clean_weight(visits, verbose = 0)

# 1. weight outlier methods: 5% artificial errors of 3-15 kg
vo <- validate_outliers(visits, reps = 1)
#> 
#> ── Validating weight outlier methods (1 repetition, 5% artificial errors) ──────
#> Validating outlier methods ■■■■■■■■■                         25% | ETA:  5s
#> Validating outlier methods ■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■                  50% | ETA:  4s
#> Validating outlier methods ■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■  100% | ETA:  0s
#> track+rlm+loess: 94% of errors found, 0.5% of good records removed, ADG error
#> 2.1 g/d
#> track: 68% of errors found, 0.0% of good records removed, ADG error 1.0 g/d
#> rlm: 90% of errors found, 0.2% of good records removed, ADG error 1.5 g/d
#> loess: 91% of errors found, 0.0% of good records removed, ADG error 0.7 g/d
#> rlm+loess: 93% of errors found, 0.2% of good records removed, ADG error 1.5 g/d
#> stl: 95% of errors found, 0.3% of good records removed, ADG error 0.7 g/d
#> sd: 60% of errors found, 0.0% of good records removed, ADG error 1.1 g/d
